ptBR.note: In Brazil the vós row does not exist and você replaces tu. The nós perfeito of -ar verbs has no accent (falamos).

rule.text: Take off *-ar, -er, -ir* and add the endings. The *nós* form of *-ar* verbs is the same as the perfeito apart from the accent: *falamos* (we speak) against *falámos* (we spoke).

The simple past for finished events: *falei, comi, parti*. Many irregular verbs have a new stem and no accent: *fiz, disse, trouxe, pus, tive.* The *nós* form of *-ar* verbs has an accent in Portugal: *falámos*.

*ter* + participle. In Portugal it is **not** the simple past: it says that something has been happening repeatedly up to now: *Tenho trabalhado muito.* For a finished event use the perfeito: *Trabalhei ontem.*
*-ar*: *-ava, -avas, -ava, -ávamos, -áveis, -avam*. *-er / -ir*: *-ia, -ias, -ia, -íamos, -íeis, -iam*. Only four verbs are irregular: *ser* (era), *ter* (tinha), *vir* (vinha), *pôr* (punha).
The whole infinitive + *-ei, -ás, -á, -emos, -eis, -ão*. Three verbs shorten the stem: *fazer → farei, dizer → direi, trazer → trarei*. In speech *vou fazer* is more usual.
The same stem as the future + *-ia, -ias, -ia, -íamos, -íeis, -iam*: *falaria, faria, diria.* Polite requests: *Podia ajudar-me?*

tenses.name: Conjuntivo presente
tenses.tip: wishes, doubt, feelings, the future after quando

rule.text: Take the *eu* form of the present, drop the *-o* and add the opposite vowel: *falo → fale*, *como → coma*, *tenho → tenha*, *faço → faça*.

tenses.name: Imperfeito do conjuntivo
tenses.tip: after a past wish, or an unreal se

rule.text: Take the *eles* form of the perfeito, drop *-ram* and add *-sse, -sses, -sse, -ssemos, -sseis, -ssem*: *falaram → falasse, tiveram → tivesse*. The *nós* form takes an accent: *falássemos, tivéssemos*.

tenses.name: Futuro do conjuntivo
tenses.tip: after se, quando, logo que for the future

rule.text: Take the *eles* form of the perfeito, drop *-ram* and add *-r, -res, -r, -rmos, -rdes, -rem*: *falaram → falar, fizeram → fizer, foram → for*. Used where other languages use the present: *Quando chegares, liga-me.*

*tu* = the *ele* form of the present (*fala, come, parte*); the polite form, *nós* and *vocês* = the subjunctive (*fale, falemos, falem*); *vós* = the present without *-s* (*falai*). Irregular *tu*: *faz, diz, vai, vem, põe, sê, vê*.
*não* + the subjunctive: *não fales, não fale, não falemos, não falem*. A pronoun goes in front: *não te levantes.*

tenses.name: Infinitivo pessoal
tenses.tip: an infinitive with a personal ending

rule.text: The infinitive + *-es, –, -mos, -des, -em*: *falar, falares, falar, falarmos, falardes, falarem*. It is the same for every regular verb as the future subjunctive; *ser, ter, ir, fazer* differ. Use it where the subject changes: *É melhor tu ires. Para nós podermos sair.*
*tinha / tinhas / tinha / tínhamos / tínheis / tinham* + participle: *Já tinha saído quando liguei.*
Take the *eles* form of the perfeito, drop *-m* and add *-ra, -ras, -ra, -ramos, -reis, -ram*: *falara, fizera, fora.* Mostly in writing; speech says *tinha falado.*

tenses.name: Futuro composto
tenses.tip: what will have happened by then

rule.text: The future of *ter* + participle: *Já terei saído às seis.*
The conditional of *ter* + participle: *Teria ido, mas estava doente.*

tenses.name: Conjuntivo perfeito
tenses.tip: a recent past after espero que, não acredito que

rule.text: The subjunctive of *ter* + participle: *Espero que tenhas dormido bem.*
*tivesse* + participle: *Se tivesse sabido, tinha ligado.*

tenses.name: Futuro composto do conjuntivo
tenses.tip: what will have happened, after se or quando

rule.text: *tiver* + participle: *Quando tiveres acabado, avisa.*

sets.title: ser or estar: the basics
sets.lead: Who or what something is, or where and how it is right now.

rule.text: *ser* says what something is: identity, job, origin, character, time and date. *estar* says where something is and how it is at the moment. In Portugal *estar a + infinitive* is the usual way to say what is happening now.

sets.title: ser or estar: materials, prices, states
sets.lead: Results and states with estar; material, owner and description with ser.

rule.text: *ser* for material (*de madeira*), owner (*do meu pai*), what something is like in general, and where an event takes place. *estar* for the result of an action (*aberta, paga, pronto*), a state that can change, and a price that changes day by day.

sets.title: ser or estar: when the meaning changes
sets.lead: verde, aborrecido, mau, atento: the verb changes what the word means. Events, and the passive.

rule.text: With some adjectives *ser* names a lasting quality and *estar* a state or a result: *ser aborrecido* (boring), *estar aborrecido* (annoyed); *ser mau* (a bad person), *estar mau* (in a bad state, unwell); *ser atento* (attentive by nature), *estar atento* (paying attention now). *estar de* gives a temporary situation: *estar de férias, estar de baixa*. The passive of an action uses *ser* (*foi assinado*); the result uses *estar* (*está assinado*).

sets.title: por or para in real situations
sets.lead: para looks ahead to a goal; por looks back at a cause, or at the way something happens.

rule.text: *para* points forward: purpose, who receives it, destination, deadline, an opinion or comparison (*para estrangeiro, fala bem*). *por* gives the cause or the way: reason, exchange, means, the way through, the agent of a passive, frequency, on behalf of. *por* + *o/a* contracts: *pelo, pela, pelos, pelas*.

sets.title: perfeito or imperfeito in context
sets.lead: The perfeito moves the story on; the imperfeito paints the background.

rule.text: The *pretérito perfeito* is for a finished event that moves the story on (*fui, telefonou, durou*). The *imperfeito* is for the background: description, habit in the past, an action in progress when something else happens (*ia, tinha, estava a chover*). In Portugal the progressive is *estar a + infinitive*.

Tinha trinta anos. Eram dez horas.
Eu fazia o jantar quando o telefone tocou.

sets.title: subjunctive or indicative: the common triggers
sets.lead: Wishes, doubts, feelings and the future after quando call for the subjunctive. Facts stay in the indicative.

rule.text: The *conjuntivo* follows wishes and requests (*quero que, peço que*), doubt and denial (*duvido que, não acho que*), feelings (*fico contente que*), judgements (*é importante que*) and *talvez*. Opinion and certainty verbs take the indicative: *acho que, tenho a certeza de que, parece que, diz que*.

Mood

rows: Quero que me digas a verdade.

acho que, parece que, diz que
Acho que ele está em casa.

items.explain: diz que + indicative: a report of a fact.

sets.title: subjunctive or indicative: the harder cases
sets.lead: Relative clauses, embora, se, and how the mood follows the tense of the main verb.

rule.text: A relative clause takes the *conjuntivo* when what it describes is wanted or unknown (*procuro um apartamento que fique perto*), the indicative when it exists (*tenho um apartamento que fica perto*). *embora, ainda que, mesmo que* take the conjuntivo. After a past main verb the clause goes into the *imperfeito do conjuntivo* (*queria que fosses*). *se* + *imperfeito do conjuntivo* is an unreal condition; *se* + *futuro do conjuntivo* is a real one.

Se tivesse tempo, fazia um curso.
Se tiver tempo, faço um curso.

sets.title: Personal infinitive in sentences
sets.lead: para chegarmos, sem eles verem: the infinitive takes endings when it has its own subject.

rule.text: The *infinitivo pessoal* adds endings to the infinitive: *-es* (tu), *-mos* (nós), *-des* (vós), *-em* (eles), and nothing for *eu* and *ele*. Use it when the infinitive has its own subject, different from the main verb, after *para, sem, antes de, depois de, por, até* and after expressions like *é importante, é melhor, basta*. Irregular verbs keep the infinitive stem: *fazermos, dizerem, pôr*.

sets.title: Future subjunctive: real conditions
sets.lead: Quando chegares a casa, liga-me. Se tiver tempo, passo por aí.

rule.text: After *se, quando, logo que, assim que, enquanto* and *quem*, referring to the future, Portuguese uses the *futuro do conjuntivo*: take the *eles* form of the perfeito, drop *-ram* and add *-r, -res, -r, -rmos, -rem*. *falar → falar, falares, falar, falarmos, falarem; ter → tiver; fazer → fizer; ser/ir → for.*

sets.title: Future subjunctive: irregular verbs
sets.lead: vir or ver, pôr, trazer, haver: the stems you must know.

rule.text: The irregular stems come from the perfeito: *trouxeram → trouxer, puseram → puser, houve → houver, couberam → couber*. Watch the pair *ver → vir, vires* and *vir → vier, vieres*. *Seja o que for* is a fixed phrase.

sets.title: Irregular perfeito in sentences
sets.lead: The strong past forms: tive, fiz, disse, trouxe. No written accent on them.

rule.text: Many common verbs have a new stem in the *pretérito perfeito* and no accent in the *eu* and *ele* forms: *tive, fiz, disse, trouxe, pus, pude, quis, soube, estive, vim, houve*. *ser* and *ir* share one form: *fui, foste, foi, fomos, foram*. *dar* has *dei, deste, deu*.

sets.title: Future and conditional in sentences
sets.lead: farei, dirão, gostaria: the whole infinitive plus the endings.

rule.text: The *futuro* and the *condicional* add their endings to the whole infinitive (*falarei, falaria; terei, teria; porei, poria*). Only three verbs shorten the stem, the same in both tenses: *fazer → far-, dizer → dir-, trazer → trar-*. In speech the future is often *ir + infinitive*, and the condicional often the imperfeito (*queria*).

sets.title: Imperative in real life
sets.lead: What the doctor, the boss or a friend tells you to do. Type the form.

rule.text: *tu*: the *ele* form of the presente (*fala, come*), with short forms for some verbs: *diz, faz, vai, vem, sê, tem, põe, vê*. *você, vocês, nós*: the conjuntivo (*tome, tomem, falemos*). Negative: always *não* + conjuntivo (*não fales, não fume*). The pronoun goes after an affirmative form and before a negative one: *senta-te, não te sentes*.

sets.title: Pronoun placement: before or after the verb
sets.lead: In Portugal the pronoun usually follows the verb. Some words pull it in front.

rule.text: In a main clause the pronoun follows the verb with a hyphen: *telefona-me, falo-lhe*. It goes in front after *não, nunca, já, também, ainda*, question words (*quem, o que*), *que* and other subordinators, and quantifiers (*todos, alguém*). With an infinitive the pronoun usually follows it: *quero pagar-lhe*.
